# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.17 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16.17 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

This score comes from reading the code. It is not a live measurement. The basics are in place: robots.txt is valid, search crawlers are allowed, and the navigation uses plain links. The losses come from a missing `lang` attribute, no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt, a pricing page marked `noindex`, a blog that loads its content in the browser, and missing canonicals. No blocker applied, so there is no cap.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap (GEO-011, 2 points lost)
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers look in `robots.txt` to find your list of pages. Right now they aren't told the sitemap exists.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-6`
- **What the code says:** the file has only `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `User-agent: GPTBot` and `Disallow: /`, with no `Sitemap:` line. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 79

### 2. Set the page language and give the blog its own title and description (GEO-012, 2 points lost)
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines what language the site is in. Your config says `en`, but the code never sets it. The blog also inherits the home page's title and description, so the two pages look identical.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11` (and `app/blog/page.tsx:1`)
- **What the code says:** `<html>` has no `lang`. Change it to `<html lang="en">`. The blog is a `'use client'` page, so it can't export `metadata`. Add a small `app/blog/layout.tsx` with its own metadata.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 79 (fixing `lang` alone still leaves the blog route a Problem, so it gains less)

### 3. Add canonicals to /docs and /blog (GEO-015, about 1.3 points lost)
- **Why it matters:** A canonical link tells search engines the main address of a page. Two indexable pages have none.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` (no metadata)
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` has no `alternates.canonical`. Add `https://www.ledger.example/docs`, and the equivalent for `/blog`.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`. Plain text, valid lines. |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed per policy | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. Only GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, which matches your policy. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. Pricing is in the sitemap and nav. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your origin | Problem | Not run | `/` is clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. 1 of 3 indexable routes clear. |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7` fetches posts in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found. |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` are present | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang`, which affects every route. The blog also shares the default title and description. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are linked with plain links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has `<a href>` links to all four routes. |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | Not run | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:15`. No middleware or `next.config` found. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and all pages. There are no images or buttons, and the links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared. |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (informational) | Not scored | Not run | None present. |

## Other problems found

- `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `/pricing`, but `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. Either remove the `noindex` or drop the URL from the sitemap. This is the same issue as GEO-014.
- `app/thank-you/page.tsx:1` is correctly `noindex` and not in the sitemap. Nothing to do.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **GEO-003 and GEO-011:** a live check would confirm the blog's raw HTML is empty and that the sitemap URLs answer 200.
- **Headers:** the repository has no `X-Robots-Tag` headers, but a host or CDN could add them. A live check would show them.
- **Blog posts:** their content comes from `/api/posts`, so I couldn't read it.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the site, as `geo.config.json` says (`aiSearchCrawlers: allow`).
- I sampled all four routes in the sitemap and navigation. `/thank-you` is intentionally `noindex`, so I left it out of the scored routes.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
